claim.quote: Observation of a Hyperon with Strangeness Minus Three

date.note: Publication date; submitted to PRL on 11 February 1964 (CERN Courier).

key_value_text.quote: On 31 January 1964, he finally found a bubble-chamber photograph with just the right signatures.
key_value_text.value: One bubble-chamber event, found on 31 January 1964

name: Observation of a Hyperon with Strangeness Minus Three
notes: The paper title says "Observation"; BNL says its team "discovered" the particle, so the type follows the title (A16).

summary.plain: A Brookhaven team reported a single bubble-chamber photograph of the omega-minus, a heavy particle with three strange quarks that Murray Gell-Mann had predicted. Finding it made his pattern for organising the known particles credible.
summary.technical: A single event in the Brookhaven 80-inch bubble chamber identified the strangeness -3 hyperon, the missing member of the baryon decuplet of SU(3) flavour symmetry.

title: Observation of a Hyperon with Strangeness Minus Three
why_it_matters: The CERN Courier writes that with that single event "any remaining doubt about SU(3) symmetry and Gell-Mann’s Eightfold Way evaporated".
